faq_heading: Burnaby market stats: your questions answered

blocks.text: The boards report Burnaby in 3 parts: Burnaby East, Burnaby North and Burnaby South. In October 2026, Burnaby South had the highest all-home benchmark at $975,400 and Burnaby North the lowest at $875,000, a gap of $100,400. Over twelve months the three-part spread runs Burnaby East down 7.1%, Burnaby North down 5.8%, Burnaby South down 6.1%.
Burnaby East benchmark prices and trends, October 2026

A typical Burnaby East home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $972,500 in October 2026. That is little changed at −1.0% on the month, little changed at −1.3% over three months, down 4.2% over six months and down 7.1% over the year. Over three years it is down 16.0%, and over five years down 5.9%.
The weakest one-year move in Burnaby East was for a detached home homes at −7.2%; the strongest was a townhouse at −4.9%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,681,600) and an apartment ($698,800) is $982,800, and a townhouse ($839,300) sits $140,500 above the apartment benchmark.
Against Greater Vancouver, where the all-home benchmark was $1,068,600, Burnaby East is 9.0% below. Over the year Greater Vancouver moved down 5.2% against down 7.1% here.
Of the 20 areas this board reports, Burnaby East ranks 13 by all-home benchmark, with Burnaby South above it at $975,400 and Coquitlam below it at $957,500.

Detached homes in Burnaby East: benchmark $1,681,600, little changed at −0.8% in a month, down 1.8% in three months, down 5.6% in six months, down 7.2% in a year, down 10.1% in three years and up 1.6% in five. That is 5.3% below the detached benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,775,200).

Townhouse homes in Burnaby East: benchmark $839,300, down 2.2% in a month, down 2.3% in three months, down 1.5% in six months, down 4.9% in a year, down 6.8% in three years and up 12.5% in five. That is 16.6% below the townhouse benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,006,500).

Apartment homes in Burnaby East: benchmark $698,800, little changed at −1.3% in a month, down 2.0% in three months, down 3.8% in six months, down 7.1% in a year, down 13.9% in three years and down 3.3% in five. That is 3.8% above the apartment benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($673,400).

blocks.text: In dollars, the typical Burnaby East home is worth about $74,300 less than in October 2025, when the benchmark was near $1,046,800. By type, detached homes lost about $130,500, from $1,812,100 to $1,681,600, townhouses lost about $43,200, from $882,500 to $839,300, and apartments lost about $53,400, from $752,200 to $698,800 over those twelve months. Further back, the benchmark was near $1,015,100 six months ago and near $1,157,700 three years ago, so today's figure sits about $42,600 below the six-month mark and about $185,200 below the three-year mark. Against Greater Vancouver, the Burnaby East benchmark is about $96,100 below the regional $1,068,600; a year earlier the difference was about $80,400 below.
Burnaby sales at a glance, past 12 months

Over the past year, 495 Burnaby houses sold at a median of $1.85M (middle half $1.6M to $2.25M), half of them within 28 days. 1,656 condos sold at a median of $647,500 (middle half $540,000 to $768,250), half within 29 days. Quarter by quarter, the median house price eased from $1.98M to $1.8M between November–January and August–October (105 and 121 sales).

faq.q: What is the benchmark price of a home in Burnaby?
faq.a: In October 2026, a typical Burnaby East home was $972,500, with detached at $1,681,600. In October 2026, a typical Burnaby North home was $875,000, with detached at $1,795,200. In October 2026, a typical Burnaby South home was $975,400, with detached at $1,904,400.

faq.q: Are Burnaby home prices rising or falling?
faq.a: Burnaby East is down 7.1% over twelve months and little changed at −1.3% over three months. Burnaby North is down 5.8% over twelve months and down 1.8% over three months. Burnaby South is down 6.1% over twelve months and down 1.5% over three months.

faq.q: Can I book a private showing with Jared?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: How do I find out what my home is worth?
faq.a: Jared prepares a home evaluation from recent comparable sales and the condition of your home. Contact him on 604-928-1361 or through the form on this site to arrange one.
